title: Amazon EC2 M8in, M8idn, M8ib, M8idb instances are now available in additional regions
summary: Discover more about what's new at AWS with Amazon EC2 M8in, M8idn, M8ib, M8idb instances are now available in additional regions
body_text: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) M8in, M8idn network optimized, and M8ib, M8idb EBS optimized instances are available in the AWS US East (Ohio), Europe (Ireland), and Asia Pacific (Tokyo) regions. The new instances are powered by custom sixth generation Intel Xeon Scalable processors available only on AWS and deliver up to 43% higher performance compared to previous generation instances. These instances also feature the latest sixth generation AWS Nitro cards. M8in, M8idn instances deliver 600 Gbps network bandwidth, the highest network bandwidth among enhanced networking EC2 instances, and are ideal for workloads such as real-time big data analytics, distributed web scale in-memory caches, caching fleets for AI/ML clusters, and Telco applications such as 5G User Plane Function (UPF). M8ib, M8idb instances deliver up to 300Gbps EBS bandwidth, the highest among non-accelerated compute EC2 instances, and are best suited for workloads that benefit from high block storage performance, such as high-performance file systems and NoSQL databases. M8idn instances are ideal for network-intensive workloads that benefit from low-latency local storage, such as distributed compute, data analytics, and high-performance file systems. M8idb instances are ideal for storage-intensive workloads such as large commercial databases, data lakes, and NoSQL databases that benefit from both high EBS throughput and low-latency local NVMe storage. M8in, M8idn, M8ib, M8idb instances are available in US East (N. Virginia, Ohio), US West (Oregon), Europe (Ireland), Asia Pacific (Tokyo), and Europe (Spain) regions, via Savings Plans, On-Demand, and Spot instances. For more information, visit the Amazon EC2 M8i instance page.

title: Fast workflows and diverse content: How AI is transforming radio production
summary: In radio and audio production, artificial intelligence (AI) is already showing what it can achieve—simplifying work for editors, radically accelerating workflows, and enabling services that were previously unthinkable.
body_text: Key topics in this blog Speech-to-text on a new level Archives become treasure troves What the future could bring In radio and audio production, artificial intelligence (AI) is already showing what it can achieve—simplifying work for editors, radically accelerating workflows, and enabling services that were previously unthinkable. One thing is clear: AI does not have to border on magic to be a valuable asset. Rather, well-known applications—like speech-to-text—thanks to AI, are finally bringing the anticipated added value. Whether it’s endless parliamentary debates, evening-long soccer games, or hours-long concert recordings, broadcasters record huge amounts of material every day. Until recently, finding a specific, meaningful statement within this material was tedious and time-consuming. Additionally, time is a crucial factor in radio. If something needs to be reported in the next news broadcast, it must happen quickly. AI is a game-changer for broadcasters needing fast turnarounds, especially when it comes to automatically transcribing recordings. For example, in the audio editor, the generated text is displayed alongside the so-called envelope (the visualization of the audio level), where editors can simply search within the text. When marked, the audio will jump to the correct timestamp, and editors can then select a segment, cut it out, create new audio from it, insert it into the broadcast schedule, and play it—all in a very short time. Speech-to-text on a new level Speech-to-text date back several decades, but only recently, through machine learning (ML) and AI, has the technology evolved enough to offer significant value to broadcasters. Initially, only a few spoken words were transcribed correctly, but today a recognition rate of over 90% is realistic. The example of speech-to-text clearly shows that it’s never enough to simply introduce a new technology—it needs to deliver quality results before it can be adopted and used. A particular challenge for speech-to-text arises from the variety of ever-new topics, terms, and proper names. The blending of words from different languages is also challenging for the technology, such as incorporating foreign technical terms. Speech recognition systems are therefore trained to independently learn new words and phrases, and they’re continuously getting better at it. Overall, the quality of transcription is remarkable today. AI even provides a percentage score indicating how likely it is that the result is accurate. Archives become treasure troves Additional functions can be built on transcribed text. It’s very helpful if AI identifies the most important keywords and automatically adds them to the metadata. This drastically increases the usability of the content. Broadcasting companies have extensive archives that may go back to the beginnings of government records. Over the years, such archival material has largely been digitized, but it only becomes usable if it can be found. With AI, complete archives can be searched in seconds. Moreover, it’s becoming increasingly reliable to automatically determine which person is speaking and when. By combining speech and speaker recognition, it becomes possible to find a specific statement from a known person with ease. What the future could bring AI has already shown its value in radio journalism. Therefore, the industry is very open to what the near future may bring: There is great potential, for example, in the automated post-processing of audio material, which can then be broadcast faster. Filler words and hesitation sounds can be automatically edited out. AI can make suggestions on how best to cut audio material, and it can make edits automatically for podcasts, short formats, and teasers on various platforms, for example. AI can also create show profiles, help assemble and plan music, images, and videos thematically or by specific markets. Despite AI’s much-discussed text-to-speech capability, whether we will one day see AI-generated newscasters remains unclear. From the example of radio production, it’s clear that AI can be an ideal tool to support the work of creative people. It takes over repetitive, simple tasks so that editors can focus on more important activities. It helps editors quickly find the right information and generate more output for various platforms. People are—and remain—indispensable in this process. At CGI, we believe the combination of responsible use of AI and human creativity are necessary to deliver trusted outcomes. title: Why Pneumatic Component Testing Capacity Matters
summary: When people talk about what keeps aircraft on the ground, the conversation usually goes straight to engines or avionics. Pneumatic components rarely come up — which is strange, because bleed air systems, environmental control systems, and anti-ice systems touch almost every major function on the aircraft, and when a single valve or air cycle machine fails, the effect on dispatch reliability is the same as any other AOG event.
body_text: When people talk about what keeps aircraft on the ground, the conversation usually goes straight to engines or avionics. Pneumatic components rarely come up — which is strange, because bleed air systems, environmental control systems, and anti-ice systems touch almost every major function on the aircraft, and when a single valve or air cycle machine fails, the effect on dispatch reliability is the same as any other AOG event. Why Pneumatics is a Bigger Deal Than it Gets Credit For Pneumatic systems pull hot, high-pressure air from the engines and route it throughout the aircraft to do several critical jobs at once: pressurizing and cooling the cabin, preventing ice buildup on wing and engine surfaces, and pressurizing various fluid systems. That means pneumatic components operate under some of the harshest conditions on the aircraft, high heat, high pressure, constant cycling, and they fail accordingly. Air Cycle Machines (ACMs), which are central to the environmental control system, and high-pressure valves, which regulate bleed air flow throughout the aircraft, are two of the most common pneumatic components to come off-wing for overhaul. Both are safety-critical, and both require specialized test equipment to verify they're airworthy before they go back on an aircraft — equipment that not every MRO facility has in-house. What Proper Testing Actually Verifies Testing an ACM or a high-pressure valve isn't a matter of confirming it powers on. A proper test stand verifies the component performs correctly across its full operating envelope, the pressures, temperatures, and flow rates it will actually see in service, not just under benign bench conditions. For an ACM, that typically means verifying turbine and compressor performance, checking for proper cooling output, and confirming the unit performs correctly across its rated range rather than just at a single test point. For a high-pressure valve, it means confirming the valve opens, closes, and regulates flow correctly under the actual pressures and temperatures it will face in operation, not simplified stand-in conditions. Skipping full-spec testing or relying on a facility that can only test to a partial envelope doesn't necessarily mean a component fails immediately. It means the component goes back into service without full confidence in how it will perform once it's actually under load at altitude, which is exactly the wrong place to discover a problem. The Capacity Problem Not every MRO facility maintains in-house test stands capable of handling ACMs and high-pressure valves at full operating specifications, the equipment is expensive, specialized, and only worth the investment at real volume. That means a meaningful share of pneumatic component overhauls in the industry get routed through a smaller number of facilities that do have this capability, or get sent out to third-party test labs as a separate step in the repair process. Both paths add time. An operator with an AOG pneumatic component isn't just waiting on the repair itself, they may be waiting on the repair, then a separate shipment to a test facility, then a wait for that facility's queue, before the component ships back. For AOG situations, that chain of handoffs is often the actual bottleneck, not the repair work itself. Why This Matters More as Fleets Age Aging fleets and extended service lives, a pattern showing up across the industry as new-aircraft deliveries continue to lag demand, mean more pneumatic components are reaching the point where testing and overhaul become routine rather than occasional. A testing bottleneck that was a minor inconvenience when component overhaul volumes were lower becomes a real constraint on turnaround time as those volumes grow. Closing The Loop This is the gap AerSale Component Solutions' new pneumatics testing capability, including ACM and high-pressure valve test stands, is built to close. Bringing full-spec testing in-house, rather than routing components through a separate third-party test step, shortens the chain of handoffs between repair and return-to-service, which is exactly where AOG turnaround time tends to get lost. For operators managing pneumatic component repairs, the practical question worth asking any MRO partner is simple: does this facility test to full operating specification in-house, or does testing happen somewhere else, on someone else's schedule? body_text: MATERIALISE AANDELENINKOOPPROGRAMMA July 20, 2026 PDF Version Leuven – 20 juli 2026 – 22h00 CET Gereglementeerde informatie 1 Materialise rapporteert over de voortgang van haar op 30 oktober 2025 aangekondigde aandeleninkoopprogramma. 20 juli 2026 – Materialise NV (Euronext: MTLS) (Nasdaq: MTLS) (“Materialise”) (“de Vennootschap”) maakt hierbij bepaalde informatie bekend met betrekking tot haar op 30 oktober 2025 aangekondigde aandeleninkoopprogramma, overeenkomstig artikel 8:4 van het Koninklijk Besluit van 29 april 2019 tot implementatie van het Belgisch Wetboek van Vennootschappen en Verenigingen. In het kader van dit programma heeft Materialise een discretionaire bevoegdheid verleend aan een onafhankelijke financiële tussenpersoon om aandelen van Materialise terug te kopen voor een bedrag van maximaal EUR 30 miljoen. Materialise rapporteert de aankoop van 51,168 aandelen van Materialise in de periode van 13 juli 2026 tot en met 17 juli 2026. De aandelen werden teruggekocht tegen een gemiddelde prijs van 5.84 EUR per aandeel voor een totale vergoeding van 299,057 EUR. 51,168 aandelen werden teruggekocht via het centrale orderboek van de volgende beurzen: Datum van inkoop Beurs Aantal aandelen Totaal bedrag (EUR) Totaal bedrag (USD) Gemiddelde prijs (EUR) 13/jul/2026 NASDAQ 5,700 34,154 39,018 5.99 14/jul/2026 NASDAQ 9,310 55,791 63,630 5.99 15/jul/2026 NASDAQ 2,104 12,479 14,233 5.93 16/jul/2026 NASDAQ 5,400 31,677 36,324 5.87 17/jul/2026 NASDAQ 28,654 164,955 188,626 5.76 Totaal van de week 51,168 299,057 341,832 5.84 Geen aandelen werden teruggekocht via kruistransacties of bloktransacties. Sinds de start van het aandeleninkoopprogramma op 26 januari 2026 heeft Materialise 1,157,574 aandelen ingekocht voor een totaalbedrag van 5,732,380 EUR (6,686,460 USD) in het kader van het aandeleninkoopprogramma. Dit komt overeen met 2.0% van het totale aantal uitstaande aandelen. Materialise bezit momenteel 1,157,574 eigen aandelen. Het overzicht van het aandelen inkoopprogramma is beschikbaar op https://investors.materialise.com/ en zal wekelijks worden bijgewerkt. Over Materialise Materialise heeft meer dan drie decennia aan ervaring in 3D printing en zet deze in voor een reeks softwareoplossingen en 3D-printdiensten die duurzame 3D-printtoepassingen mogelijk maken. Onze open, veilige en flexibele end-to-endoplossingen ondersteunen industriële productie en massapersonalisatie in diverse sectoren, waaronder gezondheidszorg, auto-industrie, luchtvaart, brillen, kunst en design, wearables en consumentengoederen. Met het hoofdkantoor in België en vestigingen wereldwijd combineert Materialise de grootste groep softwareontwikkelaars in de branche met een van ’s werelds grootste en meest complete 3D-printfaciliteiten. [1] De bijgevoegde informatie bevat gereglementeerde informatie zoals gedefinieerd in het Koninklijk Besluit van 14 november 2007 betreffende de verplichtingen van emittenten van financiële instrumenten die zijn toegelaten tot de verhandeling op een gereglementeerde markt.

title: PhantomBuster Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs, and Comparative Analysis
summary: Discover PhantomBuster's pricing and compare it against competitors. Learn about features, hidden costs, and best fit use cases.
body_text: Title: PhantomBuster Pricing 2026: Plans, Costs, and Comparative Analysis TL;DR: PhantomBuster offers tiered pricing from $69/month to $439/month with significant functions for automating social data scraping and outreach, but beware of hidden costs and feature limitations. In 2026, automation tools are evolving with increasingly complex pricing structures. Companies like PhantomBuster provide low-code solutions for social scraping, but users are often unsure what these configurations will actually cost them. As the market matures, transparency in pricing becomes critical for decision-makers. What Are PhantomBuster's Pricing Plans in 2026? PhantomBuster offers a range of pricing plans starting from $69/month for their Starter plan, up to $439/month for their Team plan. Each plan varies significantly in terms of features and usage allowances. This pricing structure reflects their focus on catering to different levels of automation needs, but potential users need to understand what these costs entail and how they compare to alternatives. PhantomBuster Pricing Table To effectively navigate and make informed decisions with PhantomBuster's offerings, it's crucial to understand its pricing framework. PhantomBuster provides three main tiers: Starter , Pro , and Team . Each tier caters to different needs, with varying feature access and automation capabilities. Pricing Overview The Starter plan begins at $69 per month , designed for individuals or small businesses beginning their journey into automation and data scraping. This tier provides essential features like LinkedIn automation and email finding, making it a suitable choice for users new to automation or managing limited workflows. The Pro plan, priced at $159 per month , enhances the Starter features with more advanced functionalities. Users in this tier often manage multiple workflows, benefiting from additional capabilities like enriched data exports and complex email campaigns. The Pro tier is ideal for medium-sized teams needing robust automation without diving into maximal user engagement. For larger teams and organizations, the Team plan offers extensive resources at $439 per month . This tier supports collaborative efforts with features tailored for comprehensive project management and extensive multi-step workflows. It includes the highest level of service, with priority support and customized workflow solutions. Monthly vs. Annual Plans Across all tiers, PhantomBuster presents the option of monthly or annual billing. Opting for an annual subscription yields considerable savings, effectively reducing the cost per month. This approach aligns well with companies planning long-term automation strategies, ensuring budget efficiency alongside sustained service quality. Feature Breakdown Aligning with its versatile pricing structure, PhantomBuster's features also expand significantly as the tiers progress: Starter Plan Features: Basic LinkedIn automation Essential email finding tools Entry-level workflows suitable for simple automation tasks Pro Plan Features: Enhanced LinkedIn automation with more user interactions Comprehensive email enrichment and finding capabilities Advanced workflow management for complex sequences Team Plan Features: Unlimited LinkedIn and email task execution Detailed analytics and reporting tools Full-fledged workflow automations with multi-user collaboration support The delineation in features between the plans is designed to match varying business scales and complexity levels of needed automation. Companies can choose plans according to their current size and requirements, ensuring flexibility and scalability. PhantomBuster stands as a scalable solution for businesses keen on using automation for outreach and data processes. However, as with any tiered pricing model, discerning the precise value each plan brings is pivotal to aligning them with organizational goals. For those considering alternatives or looking to integrate additional solutions, our exploration of PhantomBuster's competitors offers further insights into the landscape, providing a broader scope for decision-making. Decoding PhantomBuster's Billing Model PhantomBuster's billing model is centered around automation, which forms the backbone of its functionality. To provide clarity to potential and current users, it's crucial to unpack what constitutes a billing unit within this system and how it influences costs. At the core of PhantomBuster's pricing is the concept of "Phantom Units," which serve as the currency for their operations. Each executed automation, known as a "Phantom," consumes a set number of these units. The more complex or resource-intensive the automation, the more units it requires. For instance, simple automations like extracting LinkedIn connections might consume fewer units compared to more elaborate workflows such as a multi-step process combining data scraping with email finding and delivery. The tiered pricing model further delineates costs, with each tier offering a different number of units per month. On the Starter plan, priced at $69/month, users receive a limited allocation of Phantom Units designed for smaller scale operations. This tier suits small businesses or individuals managing modest outreach campaigns. The Pro tier at $159/month provides a larger pool of units, catering to mid-sized operations that require more frequent or complex automations. Lastly, the Team plan at $439/month is geared towards larger teams with substantial automation needs, offering an expansive unit allocation suitable for extensive or simultaneous campaigns. Cost management within each tier is influenced by factors such as the frequency of automation runs, the amount of data processed, and the complexity of the tasks automated. Users should carefully plan their unit usage to avoid exceeding their monthly limits, which can lead to additional charges or interrupted services. Understanding the unit consumption of each automation type is key to estimating potential expenses accurately. For example, a user might automate LinkedIn connection requests daily, each run consuming a set number of units, enabling them to project monthly costs based on planned usage. To effectively manage expenses, PhantomBuster users can utilize the platform's internal dashboard to track unit consumption and adjust their automation strategies accordingly. This proactive approach can prevent unexpected charges and ensure that users maximize the value of their subscription. Moreover, opting for annual billing can provide considerable savings, as discounted rates are available for those who commit long-term. While PhantomBuster's billing model can seem intricate at first glance, its transparency regarding unit consumption and usage monitoring tools helps users gauge their costs in alignment with their business needs. For those evaluating PhantomBuster alternatives , understanding these intricacies is crucial in deciding whether the platform's offerings align with their operational goals and budget constraints. Competitors like Zapier, Make, and n8n provide different angles on automation and integration, each with unique strengths and areas of expertise. Zapier Zapier excels in connecting diverse apps through automation "Zaps" that enhance productivity for individuals and businesses alike. It shines in scenarios requiring smooth integration across a wide array of applications. Best for: Connecting different apps without code Key features: Multi-step Zaps for complex workflows Automations between over 5,000 apps Conditional logic for branching workflows Task history for monitoring and troubleshooting Built-in app directory for easy app discovery Pricing: Free: Limited to 100 tasks/month Starter: $29.99/month with premium apps and more tasks Professional: $61.25/month with custom logic and premium features Strengths: Strong in variety, Zapier connects more apps (over 5,000) than any other tool on the market, allowing extensive customization in workflows. Weaknesses: The cost can become prohibitive as the task volume increases, as higher tiers are necessary for more complex workflows. Choose Zapier when: Your priority is integrating a wide range of apps and you're dealing with high-volume tasks that need versatile functionality. Make (formerly Integromat) Make offers a robust visual interface for creating automated workflows, catering to both simplicity and complex logic without requiring code. Best for: Visual workflow design with flexible functionality Key features: Drag-and-drop interface for visual workflow creation Custom app connectors for tailor-made solutions Error handling features for reliable automation Real-time execution monitoring Integrates with popular data sources including MySQL and Google Sheets Pricing: Free: Limited features and 1,000 operations Core: $9/month for essential features Pro: $16/month with advanced features and operations Strengths: Make is praised for its low pricing at entry tiers and intuitive interface that simplifies complex automation tasks. Weaknesses: While affordable at lower tiers, Make becomes competitive in pricing as the need for more operations or advanced features increases. Choose Make when: You need an intuitive interface with visual tools and are looking for an entry-level price point with the option to scale. n8n n8n is an open-source workflow automation tool that allows extensive modifications and integration of automation within your own server for increased control and privacy. Best for: Customizable, on-premises workflow automation Key features: Open-source flexibility for full customization Supports self-hosting for enhanced privacy and control Built-in tools for API management and automation Node-based interface for modular workflow building Supports both simple and complex workflows Pricing: Self-hosted: Free Cloud service: $20/month with enhanced features Strengths: n8n provides full control over workflows with its open-source model, allowing tailored solutions specific to user needs. Weaknesses: Installation and setup can be technical and time-intensive, potentially requiring more initial effort compared to SaaS alternatives. Choose n8n when: You require deep customization and prefer self-hosting solutions for privacy or control, and don't mind the technical setup involved. PhantomBuster PhantomBuster stands out for its specialized focus on scraping social media data and automating outreach campaigns. It suits businesses aiming for precise automation in social media interactions and lead generation. Best for: Automated social media data scraping and outreach Key features: LinkedIn automation for lead generation Email finding and enrichment capabilities Workflows designed for multi-step automation Extensive web scraping abilities for data collection Cloud platform allows operations without local installations Pricing: Starter: $69/month with core features Pro: $159/month for expanded use cases Team: $439/month for collaborative projects Strengths: PhantomBuster delivers dedicated automation for social media tasks, which can massively reduce manual effort in lead generation. Weaknesses: The pricing tiers can escalate quickly if your needs surpass basic social media scraping, leading to higher costs for broader functionalities. Choose PhantomBuster when: You focus on social media data scraping and automated outreach as core components of your business operations. Hidden Fees and Gotchas in PhantomBuster Plans PhantomBuster's pricing plans present a clear tier structure, but beneath the surface lurk additional costs and constraints that users should be aware of before committing. These potential pitfalls can affect both budgeting and functionality as your usage scales. One significant but often understated factor is the potential for extra costs associated with PhantomBuster's usage limits. As you dig deeper into automating your social media interactions or data scraping activities, you might find yourself bumping against these constraints. For instance, each plan has a set limit on computing time and the number of operations or Phantoms that you can run. If your needs exceed these predetermined ceilings, you may incur additional charges. Users on the Starter plan, costed at $69/month, might face these limits quicker than anticipated, especially if running multiple operations simultaneously or handling larger data sets. The Pro plan at $159/month and the Team plan at $439/month offer increased limits, but the risk of surpassing those thresholds remains, particularly for businesses scaling rapidly. In addition to usage overages, there are tier-related constraints that influence functionality. For example, not all Phantoms or features are accessible at the lower-tier plans. Advanced automation sequences and certain premium support options could be reserved for higher-paying subscribers. This tiered access means that even if you find a particular tool useful within the PhantomBuster ecosystem, it might not be readily available unless you upgrade your subscription. This can lead to an onboarding experience where users think they have immediate access to all advertised features, only to discover that many are gated by paywalls. Custom integrations present another area where hidden expenses can evolve. Although PhantomBuster supports a wide range of social media platforms and functionality, integrating with unique business processes or less-common platforms may require bespoke development work. This often involves additional time and resources, either through paid add-ons or third-party developers, adding to the initial straightforward licensing costs. A potential scenario for small teams might illustrate this: imagine a startup utilizing PhantomBuster for lead generation through LinkedIn and needing to expand their outreach as they gain traction. The initial Starter plan may suffice during the early days but could quickly become restrictive as their operation grows. This might necessitate a switch to the Pro or even the Team plan, each incrementally more costly, and could lead to unforeseen budget adjustments if such an expansion wasn't anticipated. It's essential to be vigilant about the constraints accompanying each pricing tier, especially if you are considering scaling operations. This detailed scrutiny can save users from incurring unexpected fees or facing restricted functionality at critical business junctures. While PhantomBuster offers a robust automation platform, prospective users should carefully evaluate these less-visible facets of its pricing structure. If PhantomBuster's constraints become limiting, evaluating alternatives might be a wise consideration. Options that provide clearer cost structures or greater feature flexibility, such as those discussed in our Best PhantomBuster Alternatives in 2026 guide. When PhantomBuster Works Well PhantomBuster's versatile capabilities make it especially suitable for users who need automated data extraction and outreach from social media platforms. For small businesses and individuals, the Starter plan priced at $69/month is often ideal for those beginning with automation. These users typically need to scrape basic data, such as followers or connections, to develop leads and modestly scale their outreach efforts. For growing teams and medium-sized businesses, the Pro plan at $159/month offers additional functionalities, including more advanced LinkedIn automations and expanded workflows for multi-step campaigns. This plan is well-suited to marketers or sales teams aiming to enhance their reach and manage more complex workflows without increasing headcount. Companies at this level often require more sophisticated strategies to nurture leads over multiple touchpoints. Large organizations with more demanding data needs typically benefit from the Team plan, priced at $439/month. This plan supports comprehensive automation workflows and team collaboration, essential for departments that handle high-volume data scraping and outreach campaigns across multiple channels. Teams focused on extensive outreach efforts will find the email discovery and enrichment features especially beneficial. Success with PhantomBuster often hinges on the users’ familiarity with no-code tools and their ability to define clear workflows for their goals. The platform's capacity for LinkedIn automation and email enrichment enables users to gather meaningful insights and engage prospects efficiently. However, users must also use its flexibility to customize workflows that align with their specific outreach strategies. In situations where early adoption of automation is critical, PhantomBuster can be a valuable asset when used by sales and marketing professionals prepared to integrate data-driven tactics into their operation. Users evaluating whether PhantomBuster fits their needs should consider the platform's capabilities alongside alternatives like Miniloop's comprehensive outreach systems , especially when scaling full-fledged automated systems. When PhantomBuster Falls Short PhantomBuster, with its tiered pricing model, often presents a set of limitations that users must navigate. At the core of its offering, PhantomBuster is a no-code automation platform designed to scrape social media data and automate outreach campaigns. Its plans, Starter at $69/month, Pro at $159/month, and Team at $439/month, each come with unique constraints. For instance, users often find themselves limited by the number of automation runs and daily execution time permitted by their chosen plan. This can hinder the efficiency of more extensive campaigns, especially as company needs grow or during peak operational periods. A common pain point arises around the platform’s complexity despite its no-code label. New users often encounter a steep learning curve as they endeavor to set up and customize workflows effectively. While PhantomBuster does not require traditional coding skills, mastering the tool can still demand a significant time investment in learning its intricacies. This complexity can be daunting for small teams with limited technical expertise or bandwidth to devote to this learning curve. In scenarios requiring advanced customization or integration with a wider tech stack, PhantomBuster might not fully meet user expectations.
